messages:
Maya Patel: quick question — do we want the SDK to expose a client-region hint and a tier override header for routing tests? thinking names like `X-Redwood-Client-Region` and `X-Redwood-Tier-Override`. would make it much easier for integration tests and local repros.

Sam Wu: i like the testability angle but worried about abuse. if any user can set `X-Redwood-Tier-Override` they could try to route to higher-tier infra and blow past quotas/cost meters. need guardrails.

Olga Ivanova: 100%. security policy: tier overrides should be allowed only for tokens with a claim (e.g., `can_override_routing:true`). region hints are lower risk but we must ensure they can't bypass data-residency checks. also: log both the hint and the resolved route for audit.

Rachel Kim: telemetry side — we should annotate traces with: `requested_region`, `requested_tier`, `resolved_region`, `resolved_tier`, `fallback_reason` (if any), and `final_model_variant`. dashboards can then show how often hints lead to cross-region routing or fallbacks.

Sam Wu: implementation note — SDK surface options vs raw headers debate. Two options: (A) SDK exposes high-level `routing` object, and we map it to headers under the hood; (B) SDK exposes a `sendRawHeaders()` helper so integrators can pass arbitrary headers. I prefer A for ergonomics + safety.

Linus O'Connor: from product/console POV we also want a dev toggle in the console for controlled canarying — e.g., a per-org toggle "allow client routing overrides" with audit trail. for rollouts UX we can show "requests using overrides" and provide a filter in the rollout view.

Maya Patel: sounds like consensus: allow region hint broadly, lock tier override behind a claim + org setting. can we prototype headers + SDK change? Sam, can you sketch the API?

Sam Wu: sketching now. idea: in JS SDK call: 
```js
client.generate({
  prompt: '...',
  routing: { region: 'eu-west-1', tier: 'enterprise', debug: true }
})
```
Under the hood we send headers when present: `X-Redwood-Client-Region: eu-west-1`, `X-Redwood-Tier-Override: enterprise`, `X-Redwood-Routing-Debug: true`. If token lacks `can_override_routing` claim, server drops `Tier-Override` and returns `routing.dropped_overrides` metric.

Maya Patel: +1. include a `routing.debug=true` boolean for devs — but responses should include `x-routing-decision` header when debug enabled and only for owners/org admins to avoid info leak.

Olga Ivanova: add a guard: tier override header accepted only over TLS and only from recognized SDK user agents or signed server-to-server calls. also require org-level opt-in. we should fail closed: if override present but not allowed, log and continue without override.

Rachel Kim: for dashboards — new telemetry fields (as events/labels): `routing.requested_region`, `routing.requested_tier`, `routing.final_region`, `routing.final_tier`, `routing.fallback_chain` (list), `routing.debug_mode`. We can add a per-model-variant breakdown to the model dashboard. Also add an alert if >1% of requests from an org end up cross-region unexpectedly.

Sam Wu: fallback behavior details — runtime should attempt in-order: 1) same-region compatible variant (quantized/smaller) 2) same-tier different variant in region 3) fallback to other region if policy permits (respecting data residency); mark `fallback_reason` accordingly: `variant_unavailable`, `capacity_exhausted`, `region_restricted`.

Linus O'Connor: product decision: allow customers to opt-in to cross-region fallback (default OFF for orgs with data residency sensitive flag). console setting visible under "Serving policies > Routing". also add a UI explanation of what fallback entails and cost implications.

dev-bot: deploy queued: routing-policy-service:feature/client-hints -> staging (sha: ab12f3).

Maya Patel: action items: 
- Sam: PR sketch for SDK `routing` option + header mapping by EOD Wed (owner: Sam Wu).
- Rachel: telemetry + dashboard mockups to show requested vs resolved routing by Fri (owner: Rachel Kim).
- Olga: spec for security checks and token claim validation, include edge cases, Tue (owner: Olga Ivanova).
- Linus: console opt-in wireframes + help text, Fri (owner: Linus O'Connor).

Sam Wu: will do. quick example cURL for QA: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Client-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Tier-Override: enterprise" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

Rachel Kim: logging note — include `routing.final_model_variant` in access logs so infra can aggregate per-variant token costs. avoid PII.

Olga Ivanova: also add an audit event when tier override is used (who, when, token id, org). important for compliance.

Maya Patel: perfect. i'll follow up with a short doc summarizing the design once PRs are up. thanks all :thumbsup:

Sam Wu: one more thing — for debug mode, we should surface `x-routing-decision` header that looks like: `region=eu-west-1;tier=enterprise;variant=opt-1;fallback=none` so clients can see the final decision. only returned if the requestor is allowed to see routing debug.

Linus O'Connor: re: rollout UX — show percentage of traffic using overrides and allow temporary throttles (e.g., cap override-routed qps for safety).

Maya Patel: noted. closing thread once PRs linked here.
